## Simple explanation

Model compression makes a model smaller or cheaper to run. This can help
deploy it on devices with limited memory, reduce serving costs, or improve
response speed.

## Technical explanation

Compression is an umbrella for techniques such as quantization, pruning,
knowledge distillation, low-rank factorization, and parameter sharing. These
methods reduce representation size, parameter count, or computation in
different ways and may require additional training or calibration.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

A model that performs well but exceeds deployment memory, latency, or energy
budgets may not be usable. Compression can improve deployability, but
engineers must measure the compressed model on target hardware and check
whether quality changes are acceptable.

## How it works

Choose a resource constraint, apply a compression method, then evaluate
quality and runtime behavior. Quantization uses lower-precision values;
pruning removes or sparsifies parameters; distillation trains a smaller
student from a larger teacher. Methods can be combined, but their effects are
not always additive.

## Practical example

A mobile vision application may quantize a model and prune redundant
connections to fit within a memory budget. The team compares accuracy,
latency, and size on the actual device before release.

## Common misconceptions

- Smaller file size does not necessarily mean faster inference on every device.
- Compression can reduce accuracy or change failure modes.
- Compression is not one single algorithm; different methods trade off size, speed, and quality differently.
